subject: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up (Lumina Labs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@lumina.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@lumina.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:10:00Z
Subject: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up (Lumina Labs)

Hi Jessica / Amit 

Thanks again for the call earlier  good to learn more about Lumina's roadmap and the mix of cloud + on-prem inference you run today. As promised, a short recap and recommended next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for migration.

Summary of your current state (from the call):
- Production: primary usage against OpenAI API for customer-facing features.
- Sensitive workloads (PHI/PII): handled on a legacy GPU cluster managed by your infra team.
- Volume: ~1.2k avg QPS/day, peaks around 25 RPS.
- Latency target: <250ms for interactive flows.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; HIPAA applicability for a subset of customers.

Deployment mode considerations (recommendations):
- Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest path for low-friction migration; best if data residency/compliance is not required and you want minimal ops overhead.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): good fit if you need predictable throughput & cost with isolated GPU pools  supports higher sustained RPS with SLAs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended for HIPAA-level controls and full network isolation  we can package a private control plane or on-prem deployment depending on your policy.

Open questions for technical qualification (please reply inline or provide doc):
1) Which specific endpoints are HIPAA-bound vs. OK to run on hosted?
2) Peak concurrent requests and average sequence length per request (tokens) for your top 3 routes.
3) Any required encryption/HSM/KMS integrations or customer-managed keys?
4) Procurement timeline and decision criteria (pricing / SLA / security evidence).

Attachments: redwood-sow-v1.pdf (high-level SOW & deployment options), soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 coverage overview).

Suggested next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with our Infra/Security (Dev Patel) to validate network/KMS needs and migration plan.
- Solutions call to review capacity sizing & pricing (Rishi will join).
- Draft mutual action plan with milestones for pilot -> production.

Proposed times: Wed 10/13 10am PT or Thu 10/14 2pm PT  let me know which works or share times that do.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call to walk through the SOW and sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jessica Park <jessica@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@lumina.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T02:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up (Lumina Labs)

Hi Marissa 

Thanks  the recap looks accurate. Quick answers inline:

- HIPAA-bound endpoints: the clinical notes ingestion & PHI redaction pipeline must stay in a compliant environment. Customer-facing summarization can be considered for hosted if we can guarantee no retention and proper access controls.
- Peak/avg: avg ~1,200 QPS/day (spiky usage), peak bursts ~25 RPS for a ~20s window when batch jobs kick off. Average tokens per request: ~1,500 input / 500 output for the clinical pipeline; ~400 total for customer-facing flows.
- KMS: We currently use AWS KMS with CMKs; would prefer customer-managed keys for any private deployment.
- Timeline: procurement + legal aiming to finalize vendor in the next 68 weeks. Pilot target: Nov 2026.

Interest: we'd like to evaluate Dedicated vs Private VPC. Hosted API is attractive for speed but only for non-PHI routes. Can you share ballpark pricing for a Dedicated reserved 816 GPU pool vs Private deployment? Also need details on migration support (data transfer, model parity checks, eval runs).

We'd like to set the technical deep-dive next week  Wed 10/13 10am PT works for me.

Thanks,
Jessica Park
Head of ML Platform, Lumina Labs
jessica@lumina.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@lumina.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up (Lumina Labs)

Great  thanks for the detail, Jessica. Looping in Rishi for pricing/capacity and Dev for security/ops so we can scope a pilot and map the migration tasks.

Short responses and proposed plan:
- Hosted: use for non-PHI routes immediately (fastest). We'll ensure no retention and request-level flags to avoid caching.
- Dedicated (recommended for pilot with high throughput): reserved pool gives you predictable RP/S and better unit cost. For 816 GPUs we can size for your peak and run a short benchmark next week to confirm.
- Private VPC/on-prem: required for HIPAA-bound routes; we support both VPC-based private control plane and a containerized on-prem package depending on your infra constraints. KMS with customer CMKs is supported.

What we'll cover on the deep-dive (Wed 10/13 10am PT):
- Network & KMS integration checklist (Dev)
- Capacity sizing & cost estimates for Dedicated (Rishi)
- Migration plan: model parity, tokenization, prompt templates, latency benchmarking, and data migration approach.

Action items before the call (assignments):
- Jessica: share an inventory of routes and which are HIPAA-bound (sheet or doc).
- Lumina infra: top-of-stack network diagram (for VPC prep).
- Rishi/Marissa: prepare a high-level cost estimate and benchmark plan.
- Dev: bring the SOC 2 + HIPAA support notes and KMS integration checklist.

We'll attach a draft SOW and a SOC2 summary to the invite  take a look and we can iterate.

Thanks  see you on Wed 10/13 10am PT.

 Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
